title: Where should an extra £250k go?
summary: Spend £250k of £250k; expected annual loss falls from £3502k to £2488k (−£1013k).

title: Where can £250k be cut with the least impact?
summary: Cut £320k; expected annual loss rises from £3502k to £3532k (+£30k).

title: The five most exposed business processes, and three things to do for each
summary: Pick, pack and ship (£1645k a year); Take an order and payment (£1043k a year); Release software (£915k a year); Customer sign-in (£663k a year); Marketing email (£350k a year).

title: The most recurring issues, and why they keep recurring
summary: 38 incidents in twelve months come from 8 recurring causes; the top three are Credential stuffing on customer login (9), Bot surges at checkout (7), Expired TLS certificates (6).

title: Accepted risks to revisit now
summary: 8 accepted risks are touched by the three events (9 links); their acceptances were made on assumptions that have since changed.

title: Controls that are now cheaper: deploy them further at the same cost
summary: Hardware keys for staff with production access from 40 of 140 to 133 of 140 (−£352k a year); Passkeys for customers from 1 of 3 to 3 of 3 (−£321k a year), at flat cost.

title: Minimum viable business processes, and the worst plausible scenario they cannot withstand
summary: The minimum viable processes are take an order and payment, customer sign-in, pick, pack and ship. The most severe plausible scenario they cannot withstand is "Ransomware in the warehouse system": it stops pick, pack and ship, about £2278k at peak.

title: The ten suppliers whose five-day outage would hurt customers most
summary: The top three: Northwind Cloud (£2848k), CrateWorks (£2848k), PayRail (£1543k).

title: The humans and agents with the largest blast radius, including their extended graph of privileges
summary: Of 100 identities, the largest blast radius belongs to identity admins and deploy agents, mostly through what they can assume or the secrets they can read. 29 of 40 agents can reach systems beyond what their behaviour policy says they need.

title: The digital channels whose loss would cost most over the busiest five days
summary: Web store £1260k, Mobile app £853k, Marketplace listings £675k, Phone orders £60k, over the five days from Black Friday to Cyber Monday.
